actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote. (text: 3/10/2025 CR H1055)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote. (text: 3/10/2025 CR H1055)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H1127)

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Green (TN) objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1692.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H1055-1056)
Mr. Green (TN) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology.
Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects Department of Homeland Security contracting officers, technology vendors, and entities engaging in research and development projects with DHS.
dimensions.evidence: amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to enable secure and trustworthy technology through other transaction contracting authority

dimensions.assessment: Expands flexible contracting mechanisms and increases transparency by lowering the contract reporting threshold from $4 million to $1 million.
Does not appropriate new funds or specify budget allocations, though it governs existing contract values.
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 and the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 regarding procurement exemptions and notification duties.
dimensions.evidence: Until September 30, 2028, and subject to subsection (c)

dimensions.assessment: Extends pilot program authorities through September 30, 2028 (a four-year extension).
dimensions.evidence: Until September 30, 2028, and subject to subsection (c)

missing_information: The exact volume or financial total of contracts that will be affected by lowering the reporting threshold to $1 million is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill extends the Department of Homeland Security's 'other transaction' contracting authority for research and development through September 30, 2028, introduces congressional notification requirements for artificial intelligence projects, and lowers public contract reporting thresholds.
